title: Canonical scalar-tower endofunctors, transitions and computation morphisms
statement:
Let $C$ be an essentially small site and use its module-sheaf categories $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ for commutative ring sheaves $R$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix presentations $p_a$ for every ring map $a:R\to S$ and normalized successive-extension data $N$ [def-weil-pbc-successive-derived-quotient-data]. Write $E_a=p_a.\mathrm{ordinary}$, $L_a=p_a.\mathrm{derived}$, $\operatorname{Res}_a$ for the recorded ordinary restriction, and $r_a=N.\mathrm{right}(a)$ for derived restriction. Define $O_a=\operatorname{Res}_a\circ E_a$ (ordinaryEnd), $D_a=r_a\circ L_a$ (derivedEnd), and $q_R=Q_{h,R}\circ\pi_R$ (localize), where $\pi_R$ is the homotopy quotient.

For ring maps $a:R\to S$, $b:S\to T$, $a':R\to T$ and an equality $h:b\circ a=a'$, define ordinaryStep $O_a\to O_{a'}$ by inserting the ordinary adjunction unit for $b$ after $E_a$, then the normalized ordinary composition isomorphism $E_bE_a\cong E_{a'}$, restricting along $b$ and $a$, and finally using the normalized restriction compositor $\operatorname{Res}_a\operatorname{Res}_b\cong\operatorname{Res}_{a'}$ (transported by $h$). Define derivedStep $D_a\to D_{a'}$ by the identical composite with $L$, $r$, the derived adjunction unit, the derived scalar compositor and the derived restriction compositor from $N$.

For every cochain complex $P$ of $R$-modules, define computation $D_a(q_RP)\to q_R(O_aP)$ as the composite of $r_a$ applied to the universal derived counit of $p_a$ at $\pi_RP$, the factorization $r_a\circ Q_{h,S}\cong Q_{h,R}\circ(\operatorname{Res}_a)_h$ from $N$, and $Q_{h,R}$ applied to the canonical comparison between passage to homotopy categories and composition of $E_a$ with $\operatorname{Res}_a$. Here $O_aP$ is the termwise ordinary functor on the complex. For $K\in D(R)$ and an isomorphism $e:q_RP\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, define $\epsilon(a,P,K,e)=\mathrm{computation}(a,P)\circ D_a(e^{-1}):D_aK\to q_R(O_aP)$. These are definitions of canonical morphisms for arbitrary $P$; they assert neither K-flatness nor invertibility of computation or $\epsilon$, and impose no flatness, surjectivity or boundedness condition.
